A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MOSAIC study. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original diffusion-model experiments on MOSAIC, SD3 fine-tuning on SPEC, object co-occurrence evaluations, and extensive appendix analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds experiments on heterogeneous objects, text conditioning, perspective variations, and car counting.

M1.justification: Appendix A.2.3 adds a text-conditioned DiT variant using a frozen CLIP-B/16 encoder instead of the jointly trained one-hot condition encoder. The original diffusion backbones, objectives, and default pipeline remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 substantially expands evaluated scene conditions: counting objects with varied shapes, sizes, and colors; spatial relations with perspective, depth cues, and occlusions; and car counting with textured backgrounds. These extend the corresponding controlled tasks while retaining v1's SPEC and object co-occurrence evaluations.

E2.justification: Figures A.21–A.22 add CLIP conditioning as an evaluated comparator. A.22 compares jointly trained one-hot, separately trained frozen one-hot, and CLIP encoders. Frozen one-hot conditioning already appeared in v1's U-Net analysis; the original architecture comparisons remain.

E3.justification: The added car-counting experiment uses 256×256 images and approximately 200M-parameter models, compared with the standard 128×128, approximately 90M configuration. These are settings for an added experiment; the retained experiments' splits, metrics, and training protocols are unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds substantial robustness analyses testing object heterogeneity and counting collapse, conditioning strategy, perspective-induced depth cues, and whether grid-layout benefits survive realistic object/background variation. The earlier model-size, memorization, encoder, grid, and LoRA analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training-seed or repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The retained protocol of generating 50 samples per condition is unchanged.

E6.justification: Retained results are unchanged, but substantial new results show poorer counting with heterogeneous objects, conditioning-dependent gains with persistent compositional failures, and spatial performance under perspective variation. Table A.7 adds car-counting accuracies of 0.700 versus 0.992 for random versus grid layouts at 10k, and 0.872 versus 0.998 at 100k. These are new-setting results, not revisions to v1 scores.

T1.justification: The training objectives and metric definitions are retained, with Equations 1–4 renumbered A.1–A.4. No new or revised theoretical assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same central claims about scene complexity, counting difficulty with limited data, and deteriorating generalization as more compositions are withheld. The added experiments support these claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations linking heterogeneous-object failures to maintaining consistent object representations and hypothesizing that depth/scale cues aid spatial learning. It also qualifies the new '3D' setting as projected depth cues with unchanged 2D relation labels, and argues that simple condition encoding is not the primary explanation for failures.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies Blender rendering, frozen CLIP-B/16 conditioning with example prompts, BCE training for the frozen one-hot comparison, and configuration details for the car experiment. Existing hardware, optimizer, and main training disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Radford et al. (2021) for CLIP and Karazija et al. (2021) for CLEVR-Tex-inspired backgrounds. The broader related-work discussion and positioning of MOSAIC remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 edits dataset terminology and descriptions, condenses the Section 5 opening, revises headings, and adds Appendix A.2.3. Conference front matter and acknowledgements are updated, while the overall narrative structure is retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds a substantial visual evidence suite: heterogeneous-object examples and trajectories, conditioning comparisons, perspective examples and comparisons, and car scenes with a results table (Figures A.11–A.13, A.21–A.25; Table A.7). Existing displays are retained with appendix-specific numbering and local layout changes.

improvement.justification: The new appendix controls strengthen evidence that the findings extend beyond identical spheres, one-hot conditioning, and fixed viewpoints; Table A.7 also supports grid benefits in textured car scenes. These usefully extend v1's existing SPEC and object co-occurrence validation. The core findings remain unchanged, and neither version quantifies variation across training runs.
